newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher on short covering.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended higher on Monday, lifted by short covering prompted by early gains in corn and soybeans, traders said.

"We were up early on emotion from the other markets on the disappointing rains," a trader said, referring to rains in the U.S. Midwest. "But world trade is almost at a standstill and the market just doesn't have much energy."
Floor sources said the weather outlook was bearishly construed. Temperatures were expected to moderate in the U.S. South this week, easing concerns that hot weather during heading would damage crops.
Traders also noted rains fell in northern China and in India. Those areas had seen erratic rainfall.
Rice ended 12 to five cents per cwt higher with September up five at $9.73. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 300 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 180 lots.
